units.translation: c. ᾗ κάρτος ἀάατος καὶ ἀρ〈είων〉: Polydeuces, he says, was watching Amycus to see where he was invulnerable and not easy to attack. Or thus: having observed in what respect he was superior to him and in what respect he was inferior, he withstood him and engaged him in combat. 〈...〉. Courage (ϑάρσος) differs from boldness (ϑράσος): for courage is reasonable, while boldness is with recklessness. So also Aristippus the philosopher.
d. 〈ᾗ τε χερείων:〉 or also ἀρείων. Lg

79-83a. ὡς δ’ ὅτε νήια δοῦρα ϑοοῖς ἀντίξοα γόμφοις: thus planed against each other, so that, when they are brought together opposite each other, they fit together. Or the things placed opposite the wedges; for they put the wedges into the sides of the planks for security. ὑληουργοί are woodcutters and those who work on ships. And just as carpenters fitting ship-timber together strike continuously with hammers on the pegs, and one sound after another arises, so Amycus and Polydeuces struck each other's jaws.
b. ϑοοῖς: sharp. 〈...〉. And Homer (Od. 9.327): 'I, standing near, sharpened it.' Lm (P)
c. ἐπιβλήδην means 'in a throwing-on manner'; for shipwrights throw the timbers against each other. P
d. ἄηται: resounds, is heard. Lg P
e. ἄδην instead of 'continuously' or 'insatiably'. P
f. βρυχή is the sound of teeth. P
84a. 〈ἐπισταδὸν οὐτάζοντες:〉 striking while standing firm. Lg
b. ἐπισταδόν instead of 'steadfastly' and 'immovably'. P

88-89a. φορβάδος ἀμφὶ βοός: over a grazing and well-fed cow. 〈...〉 so that the name of the pasture might give the cow a larger and greater body and beauty. Antipater in his work On Animals says that the strongest bull in the herd mates with all the cows, and does not allow another; but if someone trusting in his own strength opposes him and overcomes him, this one from then on approaches the cows.
b. φορβάδος: of a herd cow. Lg (P)

90-93. ἀερϑεὶς βουτύπος οἷα πόδ〈εσσι〉: lifted up. Standing on the tips of his feet, he says, and stretching himself out like an ox-slayer, he brought down his hand; but as he attacked, Polydeuces withstood him and, inclining his head to his shoulder, received the blow on his arm. A βουτύπος is one who strikes the sacrificial oxen with an axe on the neck; he stands on the tips of his toes when about to strike.
94-95a. ὁ δ’ ἄγχ’ αὐτοῖο: advancing near him and shifting his legs, he struck him on the ear.
b. παρὲκ γόνυ γουνὸς ἀμείβων is Homeric (Il. 11.547). P
96-97a. ὁ δ’ ἅμ’ ὀδύ〈νῃ〉: Amycus, overcome by pain, fell to the ground and perished.
c. τοῦ δ’ ἀϑρόος ἔκχυτο ϑυμός: instead of 'swiftly', he breathed out his life. Lg P
